newsitem.title: Japan: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer on rocketing JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer on rocketing JGBs.

text.p: The key December Euroyen deposit rate contract ended Thursday's session firmer in sympathy with skyrocketing Japanese government bonds, but the gains were comparatively limited due to modest turnover, traders said.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) stayed neutral in its regular market operations. Friday is the final day of the one-month bank reporting period in which banks are required to deposit a certain amount of reserves at the central bank.
After the day session closed, the government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) announced that Japan's gross domestic product rose a real 3.6 percent in calendar 1996 from the previous year.

Traders said Euroyen prices may be aided by an EPA official's remark that Japan's growth will slow in the early part of fiscal 1997/98. The remark underscored the market's belief that the BOJ will maintain its ultra-easy credit stance at least until the autumn.
But the official also said the economy is expected to pick up in the latter half of the year.

The market was also cheered by news that comprehensive measures to raise the liquidity of the property market were unlikely to be included in the government deregulation package due to be announced later this month, traders said.

The debt market has been worried about possible land remedies by the government, because revitalised land transactions would raise the prospect of a healthy economic recovery, giving the BOJ leeway to tighten its credit grip.
The market was also supported by a rumour that Daiwa Securities Co would hold news conference on client accounts linked with racketeers.
But Daiwa denied it was intending to hold a news conference. It also said checks being conducted by Japan's securities watchdog were only a routine inspection.
Trading of 30 billion yen worth of key three month certificates of deposit (CDs) was done at 0.54 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
